paragraphs: Art. 130. (1) Interpretative decisions and interpretative rulings are adopted and announced within three months from the receipt of the request, and in cases of special legal complexity, within six months.

(2) Interpretative decisions and interpretative rulings are binding on the bodies of the judiciary and of the executive, on the bodies of local self-government, and on all bodies that issue administrative acts.

279.title: Registration judges
paragraphs: Art. 279. (1) There are registration judges at the district courts.
(2) Their number is set by the Minister of Justice.
(3) Where a district court has no registration judge or he is prevented, his functions are performed by a district judge, and the Minister of Justice is informed.
(4) The Minister of Justice may assign a state bailiff of the same court to perform the functions of a registration judge.

280.title: Functions of the registration judge
paragraphs: Art. 280. (1) The registration judge:
1. orders or refuses entries, notes or deletions in the property register and rules on information and certificates;
2. performs notarial and other acts provided by law.
(2) A registration judge may act only in his district.

294.title: Legal capacity
paragraphs: Art. 294. (1) Law graduates acquire legal capacity after a 6-month internship as trainee lawyers and an exam.

(2) During the internship, trainee lawyers learn in practice the main functions and work organisation of the professions that require a law degree and take part in drafting acts and documents of legal significance.

297.title: Internship
paragraphs: Art. 297. (1) The Minister of Justice or an authorised deputy minister assigns the trainee lawyer to the regional court of the judicial district of his permanent address; exceptionally, for important reasons, to another district.
(2) The internship has two stages:
1. basic: a general introduction to the functions, duties and organisation of the judicial bodies, for at least two months, with a mentor in each body;

2. professional: with a lawyer, notary, private bailiff, another legal profession, an executive body or another institution under the ordinance under Art. 297a concerned with the development of law, the judiciary or human rights; it lasts 4 months under a mentor and may also be done in a judicial body.
(3) The trainee receives no remuneration and the time does not count for social insurance, unless the contract with the person under para. 2, item 2 provides otherwise.
(4) The internship under para. 2, item 1 counts in the appraisal of the judge, prosecutor or investigator concerned.
(5) The professional internship is led by a mentor with at least 5 years in the position or profession, in the regional district stated under Art. 296, item 1.
(6) The internship is complete when the trainee book is duly certified by the court, the prosecutor's office and the investigation department.

300.title: Exam
paragraphs: Art. 300. (1) The exam for legal capacity is uniform and anonymous. It combines a case and a practice-oriented test, graded "pass" or "fail".
(2) It checks the practical knowledge and skills acquired, including the analysis of legally relevant facts and applicable law, and professional legal ethics.
(3) A trainee who fails may sit the exam again after an additional two-month internship under Art. 297(2), item 1, up to three times.
(4) The results are recorded in a protocol signed by the commission and kept at the Ministry of Justice.

301.title: Certificate
paragraphs: Art. 301. The Minister of Justice issues a certificate of legal capacity to a trainee lawyer who passed.
